subject: Re: Pilot extension request and conversion incentives
messages:

Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@aurora-tech.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot extension — need 2 extra weeks and pricing clarity

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for getting the pilot up and running — the initial results look promising. The team has run into one blocking scenario in model throughput testing and would like to extend the time-boxed evaluation by two weeks to finish the integration and validate SLOs.

Before we confirm, procurement has two asks we need your help with:
- Clear pricing for an interim two-week extension (either as pro-rated days or a credit amount).
- Confirmation on any conversion incentive if we decide to move to a reserved/dedicated plan after the pilot (we have 10–12 other initiatives; a conversion incentive would accelerate our decision).

Can you send a short set of options today? We’re targeting an internal acceptance meeting next Thursday.

Appreciate it,
Liam
Sr. Product Manager
Aurora Technologies

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot extension — need 2 extra weeks and pricing clarity

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear ask and for sending the usage report. Quick reply with two pragmatic paths that have worked for similar customers:

Option A — Short extension as credit (recommended)
- We convert 14 calendar days into a $6,500 pilot credit applied to your account.
- Credit can be used against usage during the extension window (no changes to SSO or data rules).
- If Aurora converts to a 6‑month Dedicated commitment within 60 days after the pilot, we’ll additionally add a $5k onboarding credit and a 12% conversion discount on the first 3 months of committed spend.

Option B — Pro-rated timebox (simple invoice)
- Bill pro-rata at the current rate: $1,200/day for hosted pilot capacity (total $16,800 for 14 days).
- No conversion incentive beyond standard 8% conversion discount.

Operational note: we can include a one‑time 20% surge buffer (no additional charge) during the extension so you can run additional throughput tests without immediate throttles. That buffer is contingent on committing within 60 days for the incentive in Option A.

If procurement needs a formal addendum, I can generate a short PO-ready PDF. I’ve cc’d Marissa for CS handoff and David for technical considerations on token accounting.

Best,
Ben
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0182

Hey Liam — quick CS note on how we’d operationalize Option A if you pick it: 
- We’ll apply the $6.5k credit the morning the addendum is signed and lock in the 20% surge buffer for 14 days.
- During the extension, we’ll run two automated end-to-end tests and provide a short runbook of findings so your SREs have the traces they need.
- If you convert, we’ll include one engineering onboarding day (remote) at no charge to help with dedicated capacity tuning.

Happy to set a 30-minute alignment call post-signature to walk the team through the runbook.

—Marissa
Sr. Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Procurement Team <procurement@aurora-tech.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Liam Carter <liam.carter@aurora-tech.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 07:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot extension — need 2 extra weeks and pricing clarity

Ben — thanks for the two options. A couple clarifying questions from procurement:
1) Can you confirm the $6.5k credit in Option A is net of any other discounts and that it will appear as a line-item credit on our invoice?
2) If we take Option A but do NOT convert within 60 days, does the $6.5k expire (i.e., not refundable)?
3) We are authorized to accept a maximum of 15% discount on conversion without further approvals. Your 12% looks acceptable; can you provide concrete numbers (monthly committed spend baseline) so we can circulate a short PO?

We prefer credits to invoices — less encumbrance.

Thanks,
Procurement (on behalf of Aurora Tech)
From: David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot extension — need 2 extra weeks and pricing clarity

Hi all — quick technical and billing note to help with the numbers:
- The usage report shows a spikey token pattern; if Aurora keeps the same test cadence in the two-week extension, the $6.5k credit will cover ~1.1M inferenced tokens under current profile.
- If you plan to ramp concurrency during the extension, we can toggle the surge buffer temporarily (Marissa will coordinate) but higher concurrency increases token burn and may require a short-term rate adjustment.
- For committed baseline calculations: if Aurora targets a $75k/month committed Dedicated tier, a 12% discount yields ~$9k/mo savings in months 1–3 (we’d apply the discount to the committed invoice).

I’m attaching a one-pager that converts usage into token and cost estimates if helpful.

—David
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Folks — summarizing agreed path and next steps so procurement has a single doc to circulate: 

Agreed path (Option A - credit + conversion incentive)
- Aurora accepts 14-day pilot extension as a $6,500 account credit (line item on invoice). Credit usable during extension window only; if unused it expires after the 14-day extension window.
- If Aurora signs a 6-month Dedicated commitment >= $75k/month within 60 days of the extension end date, Redwood will:
  * Apply an additional $5,000 onboarding credit to the first invoice, and
  * Apply a 12% discount to the first three months of committed spend.
- Redwood will enable a 20% surge buffer for the 14-day window and provide two automated E2E tests + runbook.

Documents attached for procurement: Aurora_Terms_Addendum_v1.pdf (short PO-ready addendum), pilot-usage-report-aurora-20260718.xlsx.

Next steps:
1) Procurement to confirm acceptance of the $6.5k credit terms (we will present it as a line-item credit).
2) If accepted, Ben to issue the addendum via DocuSign and Marissa will schedule the 30-minute handoff.
